notes: Libretto by Lorenzo Da Ponte (1787). Words follow the Schirmer vocal score's spelling and punctuation, and its repeats of words and lines. Where the print differs from the libretto the words follow the print: "bujo" (libretto buio), Ottavio "dà" and "omai", Anna "piccolo" (some librettos picciolo), Elvira "O mio marito!" (libretto È mio marito), Elvira and Leporello both "cheto" (libretto Elvira cheta), "Una porta la vegg' io" with la unaccented (sung as là, there) and vegg' and i-o on separate notes, "Ah dov' è" and "com' era" as two words, "Perdon, perdono! Signori miei!", "quà", and "sar-rà", the print's syllable split of sarà (the importer matches letters, so the word is written sarrà; IPA saˈra). Ottavio and Masetto sing "stupido", the women "stupida". The score ends at the fermata before the Molto allegro ("Mille torbidi pensieri", the next piece). IPA, word meanings and translations were drafted for this app (S43) and the IPA was checked against Castel. IPA follows sung Italian conventions: stressed syllable marked, elisions (two words on one note in the score) joined with ‿, open e/o as ɛ/ɔ. Translation literal, for meaning.

I can feel my heart pounding,
and such dread comes over me

now's my chance to get away,
